content:
cs-jen: FYI — Acme reported their Dedicated pool didn't scale during a traffic spike. End user errors (502/504) and long tail latencies. They hit this at ~11:12 PT.

alex: Oof. Do we have the customer's scale request logs? queueing time?

cs-jen: Attached the timeline from customer metrics: upstream requests queued ~85s before we served them. They saw ~95% errors for that window. They restarted a client but still hit it.

marta: Any autoscaler events? Could be probe throttling, or service-account attach failing.

devbot: autoscaler: scale_request queued (req_id=sr-9c7) reason="capacity_limit" details="token_rotation_pending"

eng-runtime: That detail stands out — "token_rotation_pending". We've seen SA token rotation block new node attach before (mount + kubelet auth retry). Is the attach step retrying?

alex: Can someone grab the controller logs for the attach controller + the attach gRPC traces? Also need k8s events for the target pool nodes.

marta: Pasting relevant k8s events snippet we pulled from the customer's dedicated cluster:```
Warning  FailedAttachVolume  2m (x6 over 4m)  attach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "model-cache" : rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = token expired
Normal   Scheduled          1m
Warning  FailedScheduling  1m (x2 over 1m)    default-scheduler  0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict, 4 nodes had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

eng-runtime: That PermissionDenied from attach controller + token expired matches the autoscaler note. If the attach step can't complete, the pod stays Pending => minReplicas not increasing effective capacity. Do we know if the SA tokens rotated recently for that tenant?

cs-jen: Customer says they rotated keys earlier that day for security. They believe rotation was internal to them but could have affected our mount access.

ops-sre: Also seeing imagePullBackOff events in the same timeframe on nodes provisioning GPUs — registry auth attempts failed intermittently (5xx). If the init container can't pull the model artifact, pod won't become Ready and warm pool won't satisfy new requests.

alex: So two compounding issues: (1) attach blocked by token expiration/rotation, (2) registry pulls failing -> pods stuck in init. Both keep scale requests queued. That would look like scaleup lag.

eng-runtime: Short repro steps we want from support to diagnose quickly:
1) Provide autoscaler log (controller) showing queued scale requests (search req_id)
2) kubectl -n <ns> get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp for the dedicated pool
3) kubectl describe pod <stuck-pod> for any FailedAttachVolume or imagePull errors
4) controller logs for token refresh/rotation for tenant
5) paste cloudprovider attach traces (if available)

marta: Also ask them to run `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/scale/status -H "x-tenant: <tenant>"` and include the X-Request-Id header we return. That helps correlate.

cs-jen: I'm sending repro checklist to Acme and asking for the artifacts now. Also flagged as P1 due to lost transactions.

devbot: Incident created: RED-INC-3245 assigned to eng-runtime, ops-sre, and support.

ops-sre: Temporary mitigation suggestions until root cause: 1) increase minReplicas by 1-2 for the dedicated pool to avoid cold attach on predictable spikes; 2) enable short-lived prewarming (burst_capacity) for the tenant; 3) advise customer to pause token rotation while we validate mounts.

alex: For long-term, eng-runtime can we make attach controller not block scale decisions — e.g., report attach failures but allow autoscaler to create nodes that will retry attach asynchronously? We want scale decisions to be driven by desired pods, not attach completion.

eng-runtime: Agree that's a design gap. Current logic treats attach failure as terminal for scheduling. We can change to optimistic scaling: once we see Pending with attach failures, still count toward desired capacity and trigger node provisioning. Need careful safety checks for storage consistency. I'll spin up a design doc.

marta: Quick patch: relax the attach success gating for a configurable backoff window (30-60s) so transient token issues don't stall scale. Want me to open a PR against autoscaler?

eng-runtime: Yes please. Add a flag `--graceful-attach-backoff=45s` and default off. We'll roll to canary.

cs-jen: Acme provided logs: attach retries showed failed auth for 3 attempts then token refreshed and mounts succeeded ~120s later. If we had the backoff you'd have reduced user impact.

ops-sre: Noted. Also let's add better observability: metric `scale_request.blockers{reason="attach_token"}` and alert when >5 in 5m.

alex: Ok next actions: (1) support to collect artifacts (cs-jen) (2) eng-runtime draft PR + doc (marta + eng-runtime) (3) ops-sre add metric + temp mitigations (ops-sre) (4) follow-up call with Acme if they can't pause rotation (cs-jen).

cs-jen: Thanks — I'll update the ticket and post back when we have the k8s events + autoscaler logs. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime: Thanks all — assigned owners, will track RED-INC-3245.
